questions.stem: Two complementary angles add up to $90°$. If one angle is $37°$, what is the other?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles sum to $90°$. The other angle is $90° - 37° = 53°$.

questions.stem: Four lines meet at a single point. Three of the angles formed are $70°$, $110°$, and $70°$. What is the fourth angle?
questions.explanation: Angles around a point sum to $360°$. The fourth angle is $360° - 70° - 110° - 70° = 110°$. Notice the vertically opposite pairs: $70°$ and $70°$, $110°$ and $110°$.

questions.stem: Angle $x$ and angle $y$ lie on a straight line. If $x = 3y$, what is the value of $y$?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line sum to $180°$, so $x + y = 180°$. Substituting $x = 3y$ gives $3y + y = 180°$, hence $4y = 180°$ and $y = 45°$.
